requirements.text: The case must reopen and start the work actively, fixing all the mistakes did last time
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 88 AND state = 'in_progress' AND reopen_count = 2 AND account_id = 4 AND contact_id = 3 AND product_id = 170 AND installed_product_id = 22
requirements.source: Case CS-0000088 Reopened as Critical Email with Second Reopen
assumptions: Derek Blake is contact 3 (account 4); case 88 (CS-0000088) is his only closed case
start the work actively means state in_progress; closed to in_progress is a valid transition in the policy's lifecycle
closed twice means this reopen is the second: reopen_count = 2, kept from the benchmark check, although the seed holds 0
account, contact, product and installed product kept from the benchmark check; the request names only the channel and priority as the mistakes

requirements.text: originally received via email but was logged with the wrong contact channel
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 88 AND channel = 'email'
requirements.source: Case CS-0000088 Reopened as Critical Email with Second Reopen
assumptions: received via email gives channel email; the seed logs the case as community

requirements.text: a low, moderate priority rather than critical
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 88 AND priority = 'critical'
requirements.source: Case CS-0000088 Reopened as Critical Email with Second Reopen
assumptions: rather than critical gives priority critical; the seed has moderate

Patricia Miller (user 111) is the group's only manager and is active

requirements.text: sending an update about it to the manager of Proactive Case Monitoring

an update gives notification type update; status not fixed by request or policy

requirements.text: sending an update about it to the manager of Proactive Case Monitoring
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE case_id = 88 AND email = 'brian.beasley@servicenow.com'
assumptions: Brian Beasley (113) is a manager in group 11 but inactive, so a reading that ignores active status would notify him

requirements.text: A case for contact Derek Blake has already been closed twice
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 90 AND state = 'canceled'
assumptions: case 90 is Derek Blake's near match (email channel, low priority, same installed product 22) but is canceled, not closed, and the policy allows no transition out of canceled

notes:
disagreement: shape: one pass tests the reopen, the channel and the priority of case 88 in one requirement, the other in three requirements split by what the request asks; chose the split, one requirement per thing asked, with the same cells and the same benchmark check in each source.
The benchmark's first check finds case 88 by account, contact, product and installed product rather than its id; on the seed that picks out the same single row, and it is carried jointly by the reopen, channel and priority requirements.
The case's product (170, Dell PowerEdge R750) does not match its installed product 22 (product 121, Dell PowerEdge R740, in repair status), and the policy says the two should match; the request names only the channel and priority as the earlier mistakes, so product and installed product are held at their seed values as the benchmark does, and an agent that also corrects the product would fail that requirement.
The benchmark's notification check counts every update on case 88 to an active group-11 manager and expects exactly one, so it would also fail an agent that notifies both active managers; the anchored requirement tests the one created row.
The request's 'treated as a critical situation' is met by priority critical; no escalation flag or reason is asked for, so none is required.
The policy aligns an SLA when a new case moves to in progress, which case 88 is not, and no listed tool writes case_sla.
The acting user, Jose Roberson (32), is an admin whose account is inactive on the seed; the policy has the assistant act with admin rights by default, so the request is treated as permitted.
